newsitem.title: CHINA: China Shenzhen bank takes on forex business.
newsitem.headline: China Shenzhen bank takes on forex business.

text.p: China has approved the Shenzhen Cooperation Commercial Bank to conduct foreign currency business, foreign exchange authorities said in a statement made public on Monday.

The State Administration of Exchange Control decided last month to allow the bank to handle foreign currency loans, deposits and exchange, the administration said in a notice published in the Financial Morning Post.
The bank, based in booming Shenzhen in the southern province of Guangdong, could also handle foreign currency settlement and guarantees, the notice said.
Profits of the bank totalled 370 million yuan ($44.57 million) in 1996, surpassing official targets by nearly 53 percent, the newspaper said in a separate report.
The newspaper did not say if the profits were pre-tax or after tax but Chinese firms usually announce the pre-tax figure.
The bank's total assets reached 16.8 billion yuan ($2.02 billion) at the end of 1996, it said.
Deposits in the bank increased by 955 million yuan, or 84.5 percent, in 1996 to total 9.3 billion yuan at year's end, it said.
The bank had outstanding loans of 6.0 billion yuan by the end of 1996, it said but gave no further details.
